I graded submission s2 on quiz 0001: 3 correct, 2 partial, 1 wrong. The grades are in `grades/0001-s2.json`.

| Item | Verdict | Note |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | correct | The loop is what makes a system an agent. |
| q2 | correct | The model emits a request naming the tool, and the program runs it. |
| q3 | wrong (M6) | You picked "left to run longer, it will eventually fix the bug". Repeating a failing step adds nothing, so the loop needs a step limit. |
| q4 | partial (M4) | The count of 4 is right, but you wrote that the model runs each tool. It only requests the tool; the program runs it. |
| q5 | correct | The result goes back as the next input, and the model uses it to decide its next step. |
| q6 | partial | Choosing by name alone is only part of it. The model works from the whole description: what the tool does and its parameters. |

**What you have down:** what makes a system an agent, what the model outputs when it picks a tool, and what happens to a result afterwards.

**Work on next:** the program, not the model, runs the tools, and the loop needs a stopping condition. The step limit also matters for your budget.

**Next step:** before the next quiz, reread two sections of Anthropic's [Building effective agents](https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents):
- "Agents", for the loop and the stopping conditions.
- "Appendix 2: Prompt engineering your tools", for the tool use block and what a good tool definition includes.

The workspace had no lessons, cheat sheets or `RESOURCES.md`, so I added that article to a new `RESOURCES.md` and used it for every pointer. The grade reviewer took two passes. The first found 5 issues, mostly pointers aimed at the wrong section, and all were fixed. The second found none.

I also wrote `review-records/0001-s2-grade.md` and `learning-records/0003-quiz-0001-spaced-attempt.md`, and updated `NOTES.md`.

Question for you: do you want `submissions/s1.json` graded too? It would show how much you kept between the first attempt and this one.
